The county's heat pump rebate program has paid out $4.1 million to 1,860 households since it opened in March of last year.

Homeowners can receive up to $3,500 toward a cold-climate heat pump, and households earning less than 80 percent of the area median income can receive up to $8,000.

Program staff said the average installed system cost $14,200, and the average household saved about $640 in its first winter compared with its old oil or propane system.

A shortage of trained installers has been the biggest bottleneck, with wait times for installation averaging nine weeks in the program's first year.

The county partnered with the community college to train 46 new technicians, and wait times have since dropped to about four weeks.

The rebate fund has $2.7 million left, and officials expect it to run out by the end of next summer at the current pace.
